Business insurance

Business Interruption Insurance in Kenya

After a fire, the repair bill is only part of the cost. Rent, salaries and loan repayments continue while revenue stops. Business interruption cover is designed to replace lost gross profit and certain ongoing costs for a period after an insured property loss.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Loss of gross profit following insured damage to property
  • Increased cost of working to keep trading
  • Standing charges such as rent and salaries, within the policy basis

Who needs it

  • Hotels, restaurants and event venues
  • Manufacturers and processors
  • Retailers dependent on one location
  • Any business with significant fixed costs

Common risks

Underestimating recovery time

Rebuilds, equipment orders and licensing can take months.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • Cover normally responds only after physical damage caused by an insured peril.
  • The sum insured and indemnity period set the limit.
  • Waiting periods and exclusions apply.

What affects the premium

  • Annual gross profit
  • Indemnity period
  • Dependency on key suppliers or customers
  • Underlying property cover

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Annual revenue and gross profit
  • Fixed costs
  • Realistic time to restart after a major loss
  • Underlying property insurance

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

Does business interruption pay if I close because of a flood warning?

Usually not unless the policy specifically includes it. Cover generally needs insured physical damage. Check the wording.
